top_story_title: Citrix NetScaler zero-day CVE-2026-88779 exploited in targeted attacks, now on the CISA KEV list with a 7 October due date
top_story_summary: Citrix has released emergency updates for CVE-2026-88779, a memory-overflow vulnerability in NetScaler ADC (formerly Citrix ADC) and NetScaler Gateway (formerly Citrix Gateway) that has already been exploited in targeted zero-day attacks. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 8.7. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 4 October 2026 with a remediation due date of 7 October 2026 under BOD 26-04, and records the ransomware association as unknown. The documented impact is denial of service against SAML-configured deployments; researchers are still investigating whether the same memory corruption can be driven to remote code execution. Treat the RCE question as open rather than answered either way.
top_actions: Inventory every NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway unit, record the running build, and flag those with SAML authentication configured - these are the deployments the confirmed impact applies to.
Check the Citrix advisory for the fixed release for your branch and apply it; do not assume the build you deployed for the two flaws patched days earlier covers CVE-2026-88779.
Patch to the CISA KEV due date of 7 October 2026, not to your normal appliance SLA; raise an emergency change rather than waiting for the next window.
Remove the NetScaler management interface (NSIP, GUI, SSH, NITRO API) from any internet-facing or untrusted interface; restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
After upgrading, terminate active sessions and revoke session tokens, then rotate admin credentials, API keys and device certificates - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
executive_summary: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway: CVE-2026-88779, CVSS 8.7, exploited as a zero-day, added to the CISA KEV catalogue on 4 October 2026 with a 7 October 2026 due date. Confirmed impact is denial of service against SAML deployments; RCE is under investigation, not ruled out.
The zero-day hit appliances patched days earlier for two other exploited NetScaler flaws - last week's emergency upgrade does not cover this one. Re-check running builds against the Citrix advisory.
EPSS for CVE-2026-88779 is 0.00276. Ignore it here: exploitation is confirmed and targeted, so the KEV listing is the signal that matters.
No fixed build numbers appear in any of today's sources. Take them from the Citrix advisory and do not infer a version.

Nothing else in this window concerns network infrastructure. Three collected items - a Google bug-bounty suspension, a macOS utility and a SOC platform release - are off-topic for network device operations and were dropped.
key_actions: **Citrix** — Compare the running build on every NetScaler unit against the fixed-release table in the Citrix advisory and schedule the upgrade now, HA pair secondary first, verifying config sync afterwards.
**Citrix** — Treat the CISA KEV due date of 7 October 2026 as the deadline for internet-facing units.
**Citrix** — Identify which NetScaler virtual servers use SAML authentication; these are the deployments the stated impact covers and should be upgraded first.
**Citrix** — Apply the fixed release named in the Citrix advisory to every unit in the device group, then verify config sync.

**Citrix** — Re-audit NetScaler running versions from the devices themselves, not from the change record - confirm each unit against the build the current advisory names, not the one you targeted last week.
**Citrix** — Notify whoever signed off the previous NetScaler change that a second emergency upgrade is required, and reopen the window.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: The source describes a release that unifies AI-powered case triage, measurable SOC workflows, deeper investigative evidence, expanded automated response and new APIs, presented as a "Human-Augmented Autonomous SOC" operating model. No capability detail beyond the vendor's own description is available in this item.

headlines.title: Citrix patches NetScaler SAML zero-day exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: Citrix shipped emergency updates for CVE-2026-88779, a NetScaler denial-of-service flaw already exploited as a zero-day, with possible RCE still under investigation.

headlines.title: New NetScaler Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks Can Knock SAML Deployments Offline
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-88779 is a CVSS 8.7 memory-overflow bug in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that can knock SAML-configured deployments offline, exploited in targeted attacks before the fix.

headlines.title: Exploitation of Citrix NetScaler Zero-Day Hits Appliances Patched Days Earlier
headlines.summary: The new NetScaler zero-day hit appliances that had been patched days earlier for two other exploited flaws, so last week's emergency upgrade does not cover it.
